item.title: 🟠 Turn threat intelligence into informed action with Microsoft Defender
item.description:
Why this matters: Could affect sign-ins, MFA, or Conditional Access — watch for authentication issues.

Every new threat raises a familiar set of questions. Is it targeting our industry? Are we exposed? What should we investigate first? 

Answering those questions takes more than another feed or a longer list of indicators. It takes intelligence that brings the relevant context together and helps your team understand which threats matter to your organization and where to investigate next. 

With the new Threat Intelligence experience in Microsoft Defender, we're bringing Microsoft threat intelligence, third-party sources, and your team's own insights together around the way you work. Threat Intelligence Overview helps you prioritize the threats most relevant to your organization. Threat Intelligence Explorer gives analysts a centralized experience to search, filter, and investigate the intelligence behind them. 

Focus on the threats that matter to your organization 

A threat can be significant globally without being your team's most urgent concern. Your industry, the regions where you operate, and what's happening in your environment all shape what deserves attention.

item.title: 🟠 Troubleshoot Hyper-V guarded fabrics and shielded VMs
item.description:
Why this matters: Credential/phishing risk — reinforce MFA and watch for suspicious sign-ins.

Use this FAQ when a guarded fabric can't be deployed, a host can't attest, a shielded virtual machine (VM) can't be provisioned or started, or an operation such as migration, servicing, or recovery fails. It accompanies the Microsoft Learn module: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/guarded-fabric-shielded-virtual-machines/

 

Warning

Don't use TPM clearing, an unrelated new or local KP, disabled Secure Boot or CI, a weaker attestation mode, certificate-validation bypasses, or copied owner private keys as generic troubleshooting fixes. Don't delete protected VM state or checkpoint files to make an error disappear. These actions can weaken the trust boundary or permanently remove access to encrypted data.
